description:

Submit to CRAN:

* [ ] Slack link to blog post, bluesky, and linkedin in #open-source-comms

title: Valgrind: conditional jump or move depends on uninitialised value
description:
## Summary     

Valgrind reports "conditional jump or move depends on uninitialised value" during `ActorId` comparisons in `PatchLog::migrate_actors`. The root cause is that `ActorId` wraps `TinyVec<[u8; 16]>`, whose `Inline(ArrayVec<[u8; 16]>)` variant has uninitialised padding bytes in the backing array when fewer than 16 bytes are stored. When the compiler inlines the derived `PartialEq`/`Ord` implementations, it can emit wide loads that read this padding alongside valid data.

## Valgrind output

   ```
   ==1246818== Conditional jump or move depends on uninitialised value(s)
   ==1246818==    at 0x178EEAA9:
   automerge::patches::patch_log::PatchLog::migrate_actors
   ==1246818==    by 0x1786FDDE:
   automerge::op_set2::change::batch::BatchApply::apply
   ==1246818==    by 0x179399F6:
   automerge::automerge::Automerge::apply_changes_log_patches
   ==1246818==    by 0x1793BC19:
   automerge::automerge::Automerge::merge_and_log_patches
   ==1246818==  Uninitialised value was created by a stack allocation
   ==1246818==    at 0x178EDBCA:
   automerge::patches::patch_log::PatchLog::migrate_actors
   ```

Triggered by a merge operation that calls `migrate_actors`, which compares `ActorId` values via `==` and `<` (`a == b`, `b < a`, `&self.actors != others`).

## Root cause

`ActorId` in `src/types.rs` is defined as:

```rust
 #[derive(Eq, PartialEq, Hash, Clone, PartialOrd, Ord)]
 pub struct ActorId(TinyVec<[u8; 16]>);
 ```

`TinyVec<[u8; 16]>` is an enum with two variants:
 - `Inline(ArrayVec<[u8; 16]>)` — up to 16 bytes stored on the stack
 - `Heap(Vec<u8>)` — heap-allocated for longer IDs

When the `Inline` variant stores fewer than 16 bytes, the remaining bytes in the `[u8; 16]` backing array are uninitialised. The derived comparison traits inline through `TinyVec`'s `PartialEq`/`Ord` → `Deref` → `ArrayVec::deref()`, and the compiler can emit wide (e.g. SIMD 16-byte) loads of the backing array that touch uninitialised padding before trimming to the actual length.
